A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SceneGenAgent and SceneInstruct. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original industrial scene-generation results, fine-tuning comparisons, and ablations in Tables 2–3, Figure 3, and Appendix A.1.

after.justification: V3 retains original scene-generation experiments and reports additional results, including the adapted Holodeck planner comparison in Appendix A.1 and Table 4.

M1.justification: The retrieval, layout extraction, placement assignment, iterative verification, C# generation, and task-specific LoRA fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged. The appendix prompts confirm continuity. Replacing placement planning with Holodeck is a comparison condition, not a revision of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported SceneInstruct training corpus and the same 40 industrial benchmark descriptions across five categories. V2 Tables 5–7 match v3 Tables 6–8. The added planner comparison and scene examples concern existing industrial task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds an evaluated Holodeck placement-planning comparator, previously only cited as related work. It removes standalone comparisons for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, Llama3.1-8B, GLM4-9B, Codestral-22B, and CodeLlama-34B from Table 2 and Figure 1, while adding the GLM-4-Plus no-verification condition in Table 3. This substantially changes the comparison set.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a controlled planner-swap experiment using unfine-tuned Llama3.1-70B, with Holodeck prompts adapted to industrial scenes. It also narrows data-scaling experiments from three model sizes to Llama3.1-70B. Existing benchmark sampling, temperature, data splits, and fine-tuning hyperparameters remain unchanged; evaluator-allocation details are newly disclosed.

E4.justification: V3 adds the Holodeck planner-replacement analysis, extends verification ablation to GLM-4-Plus, introduces three GPT-4o scene comparisons in Figure 3, and describes exploratory multimodal judging in Appendix A.5.2. Conversely, it removes the Llama3.1-8B and Codestral-22B data-scaling analyses. The API-guidance ablation is retained, moving from v2 Appendix A.1 to v3 Section 4.3.2.

E5.justification: Both versions report five generated samples per description at temperature 1. V3 explicitly writes the standard estimator for the existing pass@1 metric, without establishing a changed statistical procedure. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or training-seed variability.

E6.justification: Retained SceneGenAgent scores are unchanged, including GPT-4o at 81.0% and fine-tuned Llama3.1-70B at 78.5%. New results include Holodeck planning at 28.0% versus the original planner at 73.0%, and GLM-4-Plus without verification at 60.5%. Standalone result entries and two scaling curves are removed, while qualitative cases are added. V2's GPT-4o standalone 69.0% in Table 2 is removed, not improved to 73.5%, which already appeared in Table 3.

T1.justification: The scene representation and placement reasoning remain substantively unchanged. Indexed notation and clarification of missing positional information do not introduce new formal results. The added standard pass@k formula explains the existing metric; no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: precise industrial scene generation through SceneGenAgent, SceneInstruct-based fine-tuning, and strong performance approaching GPT-4o. The headline 81.0% result and contribution scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions explain synthetic-description limitations, why smaller models require Llama3.1-70B for other stages, limitations of CLIP and multimodal evaluation, and the rationale for the one-meter collision criterion. V3 also interprets Holodeck's industrial shortcomings. Its scaling discussion replaces the smaller-model reasoning-gain hypothesis with a data-threshold and generalization interpretation, substantially expanding the paper's rationale and qualifications.

D1.justification: V3 adds a dataset datasheet covering validation-instance counts, collection timing, licensing, distribution, and maintenance; concrete assignment, verification, and reassignment training examples; object-library provenance and its 20 models across 10 types; and benchmark-author and evaluator-allocation details. These substantially expand documentation of existing work. The original prompts, training hyperparameters, and repository availability are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations and distinguishes arranging predefined assets from directly synthesizing NeRF or other 3D representations in Section 5. It also adds agent, dataset-documentation, and evaluation references, and empirically contrasts Holodeck's planner. The central positioning around computable, refinable layout representations remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are retained, with localized prose and notation edits, subsection renaming, and the Fu Ling to Ling Fu author-name correction. The API-guidance ablation moves into the main text, and appendices are expanded and reorganized around dataset documentation, examples, and experimental explanations.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially revised: Table 2 loses standalone rows and the agent-indicator column, changes model ordering and bolding, and Table 3 expands. V3 adds the Holodeck table and a scene-comparison figure. Figure 1 is redrawn with hatching and fewer baseline bars, while the scaling plot becomes a rescaled, single-model Figure 4.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly strengthens empirical support through the adapted Holodeck comparison and improves auditability through dataset, training-example, and evaluation documentation. These benefits are limited by removal of smaller-model baseline and scaling evidence and an error in the new Figure 3 discussion, which calls robots tables. The core method and headline results remain unchanged.
